summary: req.fresh (and so res.send's 304 handling) now evaluates conditional-request validators for QUERY requests as well as GET/HEAD; a QUERY with a matching ETag previously always got the full response
The HTML body sent by res.redirect() when HTML is accepted now has , and <body> wrappers instead of a bare <p> fragment
app.render(view, null, callback) is now treated like omitted or empty options instead of throwing on the null locals
res.send() keeps the existing parameters of a Content-Type when it appends charset (text/plain; foo=bar -> text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8) instead of dropping them
res.send() no longer throws when the response's Content-Type header fails to parse; it leaves the header as set
The default error handler logs the whole error object (including cause and library-specific properties) instead of only err.stack
res.attachment(), res.download() and res.sendFile() now emit Content-Disposition filenames that are valid HTTP tokens without quotes (filename=user.html) where they were always quoted before
express.json/urlencoded/raw/text (body-parser 2.3) throw at parser construction when the limit option is invalid instead of silently disabling the body size limit
